messages.task:
You are a financial-analysis assistant. You have access to a set of callable tools that let you query a synthetic database representing several real-estate acquisitions described below. Use the tools when needed and combine the returned information with reasoning to answer the question.

Scenario description (background – narrative only):
As part of its growth strategy the company pursued a number of property acquisitions.
• In February 2007 it purchased Bremner Healthcare Real Estate, a national health-care development and management firm, primarily to expand development capabilities.  The sellers received initial consideration of $47.1 million and may receive contingent payments over the next three years; approximately $39.0 million of the consideration was recorded as goodwill attributable to Bremner’s development platform and workforce.
• During 2006 the company acquired the majority of a Washington, D.C. metropolitan portfolio of suburban office and light-industrial properties commonly referred to as the “Mark Winkler Portfolio”.  The purchase involved 32 in-service properties with roughly 2.9 million square feet of rentable space, 166 acres of undeveloped land and certain related management assets.  The purchase price was financed largely through assumed mortgage loans and new borrowings.  The assets acquired and liabilities assumed were recorded at estimated fair value at the acquisition date.
• The company also completed the purchase of an industrial real-estate portfolio in Savannah, Georgia, consisting of 18 buildings (≈5.1 million rentable square feet) and more than 60 acres of undeveloped land.  Other land and storage assets in Houston were bought for $89.7 million (partly via the assumption of secured debt with fair value $34.3 million).

All results of operations for the acquired properties have been included in continuing rental operations or development services, as applicable.

Available tools (they can be called at any time):
1. list_available_acquisitions()               -> list[str]
   Return the names of all acquisitions recorded in the database, ordered alphabetically.
2. get_acquisition_id(acquisition_name)        -> int | None
   Given an acquisition name (case-insensitive), return its internal identifier or None if not found.
3. get_financial_metric_value(acq_id, metric_name) -> float | None
   For the specified acquisition ID, return the numeric value of a named financial metric (e.g. "total assets acquired").
4. list_all_asset_categories()                 -> list[str]
   Retrieve the master list of all asset category names known in the database.
5. get_category_id(category_name)              -> int | None
   Return the internal identifier of a given asset category name.
6. get_allocation_amount(acq_id, cat_id)       -> float | None
   Return the amount allocated to a particular asset category for the chosen acquisition.
7. list_categories_for_acquisition(acq_id)     -> list[str]
   List all asset categories that have allocations for a given acquisition.
8. get_average_allocation_for_category(category_name) -> float | None
   Compute the average allocation (across all acquisitions) made to the specified category.
9. get_most_recent_acquisition()               -> str | None
   Return the name of the most recently dated acquisition.

Each tool invocation returns data instantly and has no side effects.

Question you must answer:
What percentage of the total assets acquired was allocated to undeveloped land?

Guidelines:
• Think about which pieces of information you need to compute the requested percentage.
• Call the tools to retrieve those values; you may chain multiple tool calls.
• Show your reasoning steps briefly, then give ONLY the final numeric answer rounded to one decimal place followed by the percent sign (%).
